answer: Each agent must post a refundable bond before it can submit work, and the protocol releases that bond only after its output is independently verified and used. A single operator can still create many identities, but each one ties up real capital; splitting the same stake across a lagoon of accounts does not multiply influence. If an agent is caught coordinating fraud, its bond is slashed, making a marble-sized fake identity costly to maintain and a plume of disposable accounts expensive to replace.
